text:
Fizgig — LoRA & Fine-tune Studio for Klein 9B, Flux 3 Image Klein, Fibo 2.0, Krea 2, MiniMax H3, Vimoo 1.0 Lite, Qwen Image 2.1, MOSS-Image, Z-Image Turbo & Base, SDXL & Anima 

 
 Fine-tune base models on consumer GPUs — down to 8 GB. Fix broken LoRAs without retraining. Find the best epoch by eye. 
 A train · fine-tune · repair · explore workbench built end-to-end for Flux 2 Klein 9B , Flux 3 Image Klein , Fibo 2.0 , Krea 2 , MiniMax H3 , Vimoo 1.0 Lite , Qwen Image 2.1 , MOSS-Image , Z-Image Turbo & Base , SDXL and Anima — training on photos, video, sound and voices, from quick LoRAs to the full base model.
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 No GPU, or want a bigger one? Fizgig runs on rented hardware — one click, nothing to install. 
 On RunPod's page, add a 300 GB Volume disk before Deploy Pod ( how ). 
 Deploying through that link supports Fizgig's development at no extra cost to you. 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 Start-to-finish walkthrough — install, prep, caption, train, and the workbench tools 
 

 
 
 

 📰 Latest news
 - Fizgig 9.8.8 — Auto-recaption corrects your caption, and Royale renders your starred epochs. Auto-recaption's first try keeps your words and fixes only what the picture doesn't show, and LoRA Royale renders the epochs you starred in the Samples gallery. Also clip captions from several frames, smaller Studio mix saves and edited captions picked up on Continue. Release notes
 - Fizgig 9.8.7 — LoRA Isolation without split backgrounds, and faster Krea 2 block swap. Two subjects in one picture stay in one scene, and Krea 2's Faster block swap runs 1.5x faster on an RTX 5090 at the same VRAM. Also a Speed-ups for your graphics card card in Preferences, far less memory on AMD, and drag and drop. Release notes
 - Fizgig 9.8.6 — MiniMax H3 Image reference Strength and Speed boost. Studio's reference Strength works on H3 Image, and Speed boost renders its first steps at half size. Also edit references kept in their own shape, a Pillow security update and faster Captions on PNGs. Release notes
 - Fizgig 9.8.5 — Studio swaps LoRAs for the queue and other tabs too. A queued job that differs only by its LoRA swaps it on the loaded model, and your next Render swaps yours back; a second Studio tab that loads over the first now says so. Also the Windows AMD launcher's MIOpen path restored. Release notes
 - Fizgig 9.8.4 — Studio switches LoRAs in a second. Choosing another primary LoRA in Studio swaps it on the loaded model instead of loading the whole model again. Also AMD's MIOpen kernel database found on Linux and Windows, and GGUF files refused at once. Release notes
 - Fizgig 9.8.3 — Frankenstein mode: blend MiniMax H3 Image with H3 video. An experiment in Studio: blend H3 video's blocks into H3 Image to bring some of its sense of motion to stills, starting from the ✨Motion preset, and save a blend as a new base. Also H3 Image in Studio and Flux 3 at bf16 on 16 GB cards, and block swap fixes. Release notes
 - Fizgig 9.8.2 — MiniMax H3 Image fine-tuning, and Studio as a generator. MiniMax H3 Image can now be fully fine-tuned, with a built-in preset and the training adapter on, on cards down to 24 GB. Studio renders any base model on its own when no LoRA is loaded, and H3 Image's Studio sizes go up to 12288. Release notes
 - Fizgig 9.8.1 — Studio's own queue and outputs folder. Studio queues renders while one is going and saves each job, Save writes straight into Studio Outputs (with Save every render), and the arrows between Baseline and Tweaked hide a pane so it isn't rendered. MiniMax H3 previews can start and end on a picture, and Delete run can keep your newest epochs. Release notes
 - Fizgig 9.8.0 — MiniMax H3 Turbo previews keep their steps. Changing a Samples-tab setting during an H3 run no longer sends its Turbo previews to 20 steps (artefacts); they keep your Turbo steps and strength, and Resume takes them too. Release notes
 - Fizgig 9.7.9 — MiniMax H3 Studio twice as fast, long clips in pieces, Continue and Loop back. On the int8 base, H3 Studio renders through the int8 kernel ComfyUI uses, so a 5-second clip takes about half the time, and the int8 video VAE works. In pieces makes clips of any length, Continue adds a clip on the end of yours, and Loop back adds one that returns to its first frame. Release notes
 - Fizgig 9.7.8 — download a dataset onto a pod, caption jobs in the queue, and every preview setting in one place. On a pod, the Start tab downloads a training folder straight from a Hugging Face, Google Drive or zip link; the Captions tab queues an AI caption job before the run that uses it; the Samples gallery lists every setting the previews render with, ready for ComfyUI. Plus Krea 2 previews on 16 and 24 GB AMD cards, and no more memory corruption from expandable segments on Radeon cards. Release notes
 - Fizgig 9.7.7 — repeats from folder names, and several captions per picture. Sub-folders named like 10 name train that many times an epoch, as in kohya's sd-scripts and OneTrainer, and caption files can hold several captions, one per line, picked at random each time a picture trains and shown a line at a time on the Captions tab. Plus a resume fix and MiniMax H3 helper previews on 16 GB cards. Release notes
 - Fizgig 9.7.6 — LoRA Isolation learns on MiniMax H3 video, Royale renders part of a run, and Gizmo's crop box follows the mouse. Fizgig LoRA Isolation and Leave the rest of the model alone learn when Automagic is picked, by switching to AdamW; LoRA Royale renders just the epochs around one you liked; Gizmo's crop box is drawn, moved and resized as you drag; photos with a colour profile train as they look. Release notes
 - Fizgig 9.7.5 — MiniMax H3 at int8 on any pruned file, and H3 Image on 12 GB cards. A pruned bf16 or fp8 H3 or H3 Image file converts to int8 as it loads, so Auto trains it at int8 instead of stopping at load. install.title: Install
install.html:
Needs an NVIDIA RTX 30/40/50-series or an AMD Radeon with ROCm, Windows 10/11 or Linux, Python 3.11–3.13, and 32 GB of system RAM recommended. Full requirements, AMD ROCm and model downloads: docs/INSTALL.md.

Clone the repo rather than downloading the ZIP (the updater pulls with git):

git clone https://github.com/shootthesound/Fizgig.git
cd Fizgig
  • Windows (NVIDIA): double-click install_fizgig.bat, then launch with Launch Fizgig.bat (its own window) or Launch Fizgig in browser.bat (in your web browser); update with update_fizgig.bat.
  • Linux (NVIDIA): python install_fizgig.py, then ./launch_fizgig.sh or ./launch_fizgig_browser.sh; update with ./update_fizgig.sh.
  • AMD ROCm: see docs/INSTALL.md.

Model files download from the Preferences tab: one Download models for me button per model.

No GPU? Rent one

Nothing to install on your computer: the whole app runs on the pod, in your browser.

  1. ⚡ Deploy on RunPod, and add a 300 GB Volume disk before Deploy Pod: RunPod doesn't add one for you (how).
  2. Wait for Ready in the pod's Logs tab; the password is printed under it.
  3. Connect → HTTP port 8081, and log in with that password. (Opened from Fizgig on your own computer, with your RunPod API key on its Pods tab, the pod logs you in by itself.)
  4. Preferences → Download models for me, upload your training folder on the Start tab, and press Start on the Training tab.

Prefer Vast.ai? The same image runs there: Fizgig on Vast.ai (guide).

Step by step: Quick start. The pod also has a drag-and-drop file manager for big datasets and fine-tunes (the File manager button in the sidebar), one-click model downloads and an optional auto-stop when training finishes. Opened from your own Fizgig, a pod runs the same version as your computer (which Fizgig a pod runs). The full pod guide.

Mid-job on the old pod with the remote desktop? It stays available as Fizgig Classic v7.x, and pods you already have keep running as they are.

features.title: Training features
features.html:
• Presets per model: pick a ✨ preset on the Training tab and go.
  • Slider LoRAs (Klein 9B, Flux 3 Image Klein, Fibo 2.0, Krea 2, MiniMax H3, Vimoo 1.0 Lite, Qwen Image 2.1, MOSS-Image, Z-Image Turbo, SDXL, Anima): a LoRA whose strength is a dial between two looks, from photo pairs or three prompts, and a slider from prompts can be steered while it trains (change its ends, it trains on toward them). Krea 2's Ultra mode trains the composition blocks only, so the dial holds up at much higher strengths. It works best for sliders trained from prompts, and with photo pairs when the change is compositional.
  • Edit LoRAs (Klein 9B, Flux 3 Image Klein, Fibo 2.0, Qwen Image 2.1): teach an edit from pairs of original and edited photos, then apply it to any photo.
  • Fizgig LoRA Isolation, on the Subjects card (every model except ACE-Step): up to four people in one LoRA, each from their own folder. Fizgig's own techniques combined with DOP keep your subjects to their trigger words: leave the trigger out and you get the model's own people, and in a group picture your subjects, strangers and people the model already knows each keep their own face. See it in action · How it works · How to set it up (video) · How to caption for it.
  • Masked training (every image model): train on the part of each picture that matters, the person and not the room around them. Image Prep makes the masks for a whole folder in one click, or you paint your own. In our tests of character LoRAs it significantly raised both the best likeness and how quickly runs got there. How it works
  • Element boost (MOSS-Image and MiniMax H3 Image, under Training Parameters): early in a run, the face and hair, or another part you pick, count much more than the rest, so likeness comes in faster. With or without masks. How it works
  • Adaptive LR: a plateau tracker that raises or lowers the rate within your Min/Max, with rollback on instability.
  • Weight averaging (EMA), on by default where it's measured to help.
  • Context LoRA: train on top of a frozen, active LoRA so the two coexist (a face on a style, an outfit on a character). No other trainer does this.
  • Pause and resume with full state, plus a training queue for back-to-back runs.
  • The trainer curates your dataset while it trains (every model except MiniMax H3). Every image starts as useful training data; the watch follows each one's loss, and only when an image stops teaching the model does it step in: throttle it, recaption it, and as a last resort set it aside. It also tells you when the whole run has plateaued. No other trainer does this.
  • Fast previews in a few steps on a turbo or distilled model where one exists: Klein's and Flux 3 Image Klein's distilled models, the Turbo LoRAs for Fibo 2.0, Krea 2, MiniMax H3, Qwen Image 2.1 and Anima, Vimoo's distilled LoRA, and Qwen Image 2.1's Turbo model.
  • A sample gallery that scores likeness live, and a run visualiser to scrub epochs.
  • Dataset prep: AI captions with Qwen3-VL, JoyCaption or Florence-2, booru tags with the WD EVA02 tagger, bilingual captions, face crops, and a Look Consistency Filter. Sub-folders train with kohya-style repeats (10_name), and a caption file can hold several captions, one per line.
  • Face backends for every kind of character: face crops, the Look Filter and likeness scores work on anime, furry and fursuit characters as well as people (see the section below).
  • Gizmo (MiniMax H3): cut clips with scene detection, crop to the subject, and record or segment a voice dataset with Whisper transcription.

Full list: docs/TRAINING.md. Everything also runs headless: docs/CLI.md.
